recipes.name: Malai Chicken Tikka
recipes.description: Creamy, tender chicken tikka marinated in yogurt and cheese
method: Cut chicken into 1.5-inch cubes. Wash and pat dry.
Mix all marinade ingredients (yogurt, cream, cheese, spices) in a large bowl.
Add chicken, coat well. Cover and refrigerate 2-4 hours (overnight best).
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Line baking tray with foil, lightly oil.
Thread chicken onto skewers or spread on tray. Don't overcrowd.
Bake 15-18 minutes, turning once, until charred spots appear and chicken is cooked through.
Optional: Broil last 2-3 minutes for extra char.
Rest 5 minutes. Serve with mint chutney and lemon wedges.
recipes.mealPrepNote: EXCELLENT for meal prep! Reheats beautifully in oven or air fryer. Store 4-5 days in fridge. Can freeze marinated raw chicken for up to 1 month.

recipes.name: Butter Noodles with Chicken
recipes.description: Garlic butter pasta topped with seasoned chicken
method: Pound chicken to even thickness. Season with salt, pepper, red chilli, lemon juice. Rest 15 min.
Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water. Drain.
Heat oil + 50g butter in large pan. Cook chicken 5-6 min per side until golden. Remove, slice.
In same pan, add remaining butter and garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add flour, stir 30 seconds. Pour in chicken stock, stir until slightly thickened.
Add pasta, toss well. Add pasta water if too thick.
Season with herbs, pepper, salt. Top with sliced chicken.
Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve immediately.
recipes.mealPrepNote: GOOD for meal prep. Store pasta and chicken separately for best texture. Reheat pasta with splash of water/stock. Keeps 3-4 days.

recipes.name: Chicken Cutlets
recipes.description: Crispy breaded chicken patties with cheese filling
method: Boil chicken until cooked. Shred finely. Boil and mash potatoes.
Mix chicken, potatoes, all spices, herbs, soy sauce, garlic paste. Combine well.
Taste and adjust salt. Mixture should hold shape when pressed.
Divide into 16 portions. Flatten each, add cheese cube in center, seal and shape into oval.
Set up coating station: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs.
Coat each cutlet: flour → egg → breadcrumbs. Press coating firmly.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry 3-4 cutlets at a time, 3-4 min per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with ketchup and chutney.
recipes.mealPrepNote: EXCELLENT! Freeze uncooked breaded cutlets up to 30 days. Fry from frozen (add 2-3 min). Cooked cutlets keep 4-5 days refrigerated. Reheat in air fryer for crispy texture.

recipes.name: Chicken Nuggets
method: Soak bread in milk until soft. Squeeze out excess.
Grind chicken in food processor until smooth paste.
Mix chicken paste with soaked bread, 2 eggs, all seasonings. Blend well.
Refrigerate mixture 30 min for easier shaping.
Form into nugget shapes (about 1.5 inches each).
Coating: Mix flour + cornflour. Beat remaining eggs. Have breadcrumbs ready.
Coat: flour mixture → egg → breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F. Fry in batches 3-4 min until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with dipping sauces.
recipes.mealPrepNote: BEST for freezing! Freeze uncooked breaded nuggets flat on tray, then transfer to bags. Keeps 30 days. Fry from frozen (5-6 min). Air fryer works great at 400°F for 10-12 min.

recipes.name: Chicken Biryani
method: Soak rice in water for 30 minutes. Wash chicken and set aside.
Slice onions thinly (not chop). Cut potatoes into 4 pieces each and boil until just tender.
In oil, fry onions until light golden brown. Remove half for later.
Fry the potatoes in the same oil until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add chicken to the pot with ginger-garlic paste and biryani masala. Cook until color changes.
Add tomatoes, green chilies, mint, dhania and garam masala. Mix well.
On low heat (aanch halki), add yogurt. Stir to prevent curdling.
Separately, boil water with butter, green pepper and salt. Add soaked rice, cook for 10 minutes.
Drain rice. Layer rice over chicken mixture. Add fried potatoes, fried onions and color/kewra.
Sprinkle crushed garam masala. Cover tightly and cook on dum (very low heat) for 20-25 minutes.
Let rest 5 minutes. Gently mix layers. Serve hot.
recipes.mealPrepNote: Good for meal prep. Stores 3-4 days. Reheat with a splash of water on low heat. Tastes even better the next day!

recipes.name: Palak Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken in creamy spinach gravy with cashews
method: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt, turmeric, red chilli.
Blanch spinach in boiling water 2 min. Transfer to ice water. Drain and blend smooth.
Soak cashews in hot water 15 min. Blend with green chillies into paste.
Heat oil in pan. Sear chicken pieces until golden and cooked through (8-10 min). Remove.
In same pan, add cumin seeds. Let splutter.
Add onions, cook until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste, sauté 1 min.
Add tomatoes, cook until soft. Add cashew-chilli paste, cook 2 min.
Add spinach puree, all spices. Simmer 5 min.
Add cooked chicken. Cook 5 min to absorb flavors.
Finish with kasoori methi and lemon juice. Serve with rice or roti.
recipes.mealPrepNote: EXCELLENT for meal prep! The spinach gravy keeps chicken moist. Store 4-5 days. This is now a complete high-protein meal.

recipes.name: Chicken Daal
recipes.description: Protein-packed lentils with chicken - comfort food
method: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt, turmeric, garam masala.
Wash daal until water runs clear. Set aside.
Blend tomatoes and onions into smooth puree.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in pot. Brown chicken pieces on all sides (5-6 min). Remove.
In same pot, add ginger-garlic paste, sauté 1 min.
Add tomato-onion puree, all spices. Cook 5 min until oil separates.
Add daal and water. Bring to boil, then simmer 15 min.
Add browned chicken pieces. Cook another 10-15 min until chicken is cooked through and daal is creamy.
Make tarka: Heat remaining ghee, add cumin seeds, dried chillies, sliced garlic. Fry until golden.
Pour sizzling tarka over daal. Garnish with green chillies and coriander.
recipes.mealPrepNote: EXCELLENT for meal prep! Chicken stays tender in the daal. Freezes beautifully. Comfort food that hits 55g protein per serving. Stores 5-6 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Chicken Bhindi
recipes.description: Crispy okra with seasoned chicken pieces
method: Prep bhindi: Wash and dry thoroughly (moisture = slimy okra). Cut into 1-inch pieces.
Heat half the oil in a pan. Add bhindi with kalonji seeds. Fry on high heat for 8-10 mins until crispy.
Remove bhindi and set aside. Add remaining oil to the same pan.
Add sliced onions. Fry until golden brown (6-7 mins).
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, red chili powder, turmeric, salt. Cook until tomatoes break down.
Add chicken pieces. Mix well and cook on medium heat until chicken is done (12-15 mins).
Add fried bhindi back to the pan. Sprinkle garam masala.
Toss gently for 2-3 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander.
recipes.mealPrepNote: Good for meal prep! The crispy bhindi adds great texture. Store chicken and bhindi together. Reheats well - bhindi stays slightly crisp. Stores 4 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Crispy beef strips in sweet and spicy sauce
method: Slice beef into thin strips. Marinate with soy sauce, ginger-garlic paste, and half the cornflour for 20 mins.
Mix sauce: Combine remaining soy sauce, ketchup, sriracha, vinegar, and a splash of water.
Heat oil in a wok on HIGH heat. Add marinated beef in batches. Sear until crispy edges (2-3 mins per batch).
Remove beef, set aside. Add more oil if needed.
Stir-fry bell peppers and onion cubes for 2-3 mins until slightly charred but still crunchy.
Add chopped green chilies. Toss for 30 seconds.
Return beef to wok. Pour in the sauce mixture.
Toss everything together on high heat. Add remaining cornflour mixed with water if sauce needs thickening.
Finish with sesame oil and green onions. Serve immediately over rice.
recipes.mealPrepNote: GREAT for meal prep! Cook beef and veggies separately, combine when reheating for best texture. Stores 4-5 days. Reheat in a hot pan, not microwave, for crispier results.

recipes.name: Dhaba Style Aloo Keema
recipes.description: Authentic dhaba-style minced beef with potatoes
method: Heat oil in a large pot. Add whole spices (peppercorns, cinnamon, cardamom) and let them sizzle.
Add sliced onions. Fry on medium heat until deep golden brown (10-12 mins). Don't rush this step.
Add ginger garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add grinded tomatoes. Cook on medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add all powdered spices (red chilli, garam masala, turmeric, salt). Mix well and cook for 2 minutes.
Add whisked yogurt. Stir continuously to prevent curdling. Cook until oil separates.
Add beef mince. Break up any lumps and mix well until meat changes color (5-7 mins).
Add kasuri methi, crumble it between your palms while adding.
Add potato cubes. Mix gently. Add water and bring to boil.
Cover and cook on low flame for 20-25 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Garnish with green chillies, ginger julienne, and fresh coriander.
recipes.mealPrepNote: EXCELLENT for meal prep! Flavors improve overnight. Stores 4-5 days in fridge. Portion into containers. Reheat with splash of water if too thick.

recipes.name: Chapli Kabab
method: Prep omelet: Beat 3 eggs, make thin omelets, fry both sides. Tear into small pieces.
Prep onions: Finely chop onions, place in cloth/cheesecloth, squeeze out ALL excess water. This is critical.
In a large bowl, combine beef mince, squeezed onions, and finely chopped green chillies.
Add ginger garlic paste, fresh coriander, anardana, crushed coriander seeds, all spices.
Mix thoroughly with hands for 3-4 minutes until everything is well combined.
Add 2 raw eggs, maize flour, chopped tomatoes, and torn omelet pieces. Mix again.
Refrigerate mixture for 30 minutes.
Render beef fat: Place charbi in iron pan on low heat, cover. Let fat drain out slowly.
Form kababs: Dip hands in ice cold water. Flatten mixture into large patties (5-6 inches).
Fry in rendered beef fat on medium-low flame. Cook 4-5 mins per side until deep brown.
Serve hot with naan, raita, and sliced onions.
recipes.mealPrepNote: Can freeze uncooked patties! Layer between parchment paper, freeze flat. Thaw in fridge overnight before frying. Cooked kababs keep 3-4 days in fridge.

recipes.name: Aalu Gosht
recipes.description: Classic beef curry with potatoes - Sunday favorite
method: Wash beef pieces thoroughly. Pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker or heavy pot. Add black cardamom and whole spices.
Add sliced onions. Fry until deep golden brown (10-12 mins). Don't rush this step.
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 2 minutes until raw smell disappears.
Add beef pieces. Sear on high heat until browned on all sides (5-7 mins).
Add red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and salt. Mix well.
Add chopped tomatoes. Cook until they break down and oil separates.
Add water (enough to cover meat by 1 inch). Bring to boil.
Pressure cook for 25-30 mins OR slow cook covered for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Add potato quarters. Cook another 15-20 mins until potatoes are done.
Garnish with fresh coriander and green chilies. Serve with naan or rice.
recipes.mealPrepNote: PERFECT for meal prep! Classic comfort food that tastes better the next day. Freezes beautifully for up to 2 months. Stores 5-6 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Nihari
method: Soak beef shank pieces in water for 30 mins to remove excess blood.
Heat ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot. Add sliced onions and fry until dark brown.
Add nihari masala and ginger. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add beef pieces. Sear on high heat until browned on all sides.
Add enough water to cover meat by 3 inches. Bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat to lowest setting. Cover tightly and simmer for 3-4 hours.
Make tarka: Mix wheat flour with water to make a thin paste. Pour slowly into the pot while stirring.
Continue cooking on low heat for another 30-45 mins until gravy thickens and meat falls off bone.
The longer it cooks, the better. Traditionally made overnight on very low heat.
Garnish with julienned ginger, green chilies, fresh coriander, and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve hot with naan. Drizzle with extra ghee for authentic taste.
recipes.mealPrepNote: THE BEST meal prep dish! Nihari actually improves over 2-3 days as spices meld together. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat slowly on stovetop.

recipes.name: Fish Curry
recipes.description: Tender fish in aromatic curry sauce
method: Cut fish fillets into large pieces. Marinate with turmeric, salt, and a squeeze of lemon for 15 mins.
Heat oil in a pan. Lightly fry fish pieces on both sides until just sealed. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add sliced onions. Fry until golden (5-6 mins).
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add fish masala, red chili powder, and turmeric. Toast spices for 30 seconds.
Add pureed tomatoes. Cook on medium heat until oil separates (8-10 mins).
Pour in coconut milk. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Carefully add fried fish pieces. Spoon curry over the fish.
Simmer gently for 5-7 mins. Don't stir too much - fish is delicate.
Finish with fresh coriander and green chilies. Serve with rice.
recipes.mealPrepNote: Good for 2-3 days meal prep. Fish is delicate so eat sooner rather than later. Store fish separate from gravy if possible. Reheat gently to avoid overcooking fish.

recipes.name: Prawn Masala
recipes.description: Spicy prawns in rich tomato gravy
method: Clean and devein prawns. Wash thoroughly and pat dry.
Marinate prawns with turmeric, salt, and red chili powder for 10 mins.
Heat oil in a pan. Quickly sear prawns on high heat for 1-2 mins per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add sliced onions. Fry until golden brown (5-6 mins).
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté until fragrant.
Add pureed tomatoes, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook on medium heat until oil separates and gravy thickens (10 mins).
Add seared prawns back to the pan. Toss to coat with masala.
Cook for 2-3 mins only - prawns cook fast and get rubbery if overdone.
Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with rice or naan.
recipes.mealPrepNote: Prawns are best eaten fresh but work for 2 day meal prep. Slightly undercook when prepping as they'll cook more when reheating. Store in gravy to keep moist.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
recipes.description: Spiced chickpeas in tangy tomato sauce
method: Drain and rinse canned chickpeas. Or soak dried chickpeas overnight and pressure cook until soft.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add sliced onions. Fry until golden brown (6-7 mins).
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chana masala, red chili powder, coriander powder, and turmeric. Toast for 30 seconds.
Add pureed tomatoes. Cook on medium heat until oil separates (8-10 mins).
Add chickpeas and mix well. Add water to reach desired consistency.
Simmer for 15-20 mins to let chickpeas absorb the flavors.
Add amchur (dry mango powder) or lemon juice for tanginess.
Finish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with bhature, naan, or rice.
recipes.mealPrepNote: EXCELLENT for meal prep! Vegetarian protein powerhouse. Flavors develop overnight. Freezes perfectly for 2-3 months. Stores 5-6 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Paneer Tikka Masala
recipes.description: Grilled paneer in creamy tomato sauce
method: Cut paneer into 1.5-inch cubes. Marinate with yogurt, tikka masala, and salt for 30 mins.
Thread paneer onto skewers. Grill on high heat or in oven at 220°C until charred spots appear.
For the gravy: Heat butter in a pan. Add sliced onions and cook until soft.
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add pureed tomatoes, red chili powder, and tikka masala. Cook until oil separates.
Add kasuri methi (crushed) and a pinch of sugar to balance acidity.
Pour in cream. Stir well and simmer for 5 mins.
Add grilled paneer cubes to the gravy. Toss gently to coat.
Simmer for 3-4 mins to let paneer absorb some gravy.
Finish with a drizzle of cream and fresh coriander. Serve with naan.
recipes.mealPrepNote: Good for 3-4 day meal prep. Paneer holds up well. Keep gravy and paneer separate if storing longer. Reheat gently - paneer can get chewy if overheated.

recipes.name: Daal Makhani
method: Soak black urad daal and kidney beans overnight (at least 8 hours).
Pressure cook soaked lentils with salt until completely mushy (5-6 whistles). Mash some lentils for creaminess.
In a heavy pot, heat butter. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until fragrant.
Add pureed tomatoes, red chili powder, and salt. Cook until oil separates.
Add cooked lentils to the pot. Mix well.
Add water to reach desired consistency. Bring to a simmer.
Cook on the LOWEST heat for 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally. The longer, the better.
Keep adding butter and cream in small amounts throughout cooking.
Daal should become dark and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Finish with a generous pat of butter, swirl of cream, and kasuri methi.
Garnish with fresh cream and serve with naan or rice.
recipes.mealPrepNote: KING of meal prep! Daal Makhani is BETTER the next day. Make a big batch - stores 6-7 days. Freezes for months. Add cream when reheating for restaurant-quality taste.

recipes.name: Brown Rice Pulao
recipes.description: Fragrant rice base for meal prep - goes with everything
method: Wash basmati rice 3-4 times until water runs clear. Soak for 30 mins, then drain.
Heat oil/ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add whole spices (cumin, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf, cloves).
Let spices sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced onions. Fry until golden and caramelized (8-10 mins).
Add drained rice. Gently stir to coat rice with oil. Toast for 2 mins.
Add hot water - use 1.5x the amount of rice (e.g., 4.5 cups water for 3 cups rice).
Add salt to taste. Bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat to lowest setting. Cover tightly with lid.
Cook for 15-18 mins without opening lid. Rice will steam perfectly.
Turn off heat. Let rice rest covered for 5 mins.
Add frozen peas on top, cover again for 2 mins to warm through.
Fluff gently with fork. Remove whole spices if preferred. Garnish with fried onions.
recipes.mealPrepNote: STAPLE for meal prep! Make a big batch every week. Perfect with any curry. Stores 5-6 days. Reheat with splash of water. Freezes for 2 months in portions.

breakfast.name: Eggs with Paratha
breakfast.directions: 1. Heat paratha on tawa until golden on both sides. 2. Scramble or fry 2-3 eggs with salt and pepper. 3. Serve hot with green chutney or ketchup.

breakfast.name: Eggs with Bagel
breakfast.directions: 1. Toast bagel until golden. 2. Spread cream cheese on both halves. 3. Fry or scramble 2 eggs. 4. Place eggs on bagel and serve.

breakfast.name: Oats with Protein Powder
breakfast.directions: 1. Cook 1 cup oats with milk for 3-4 mins. 2. Let cool slightly, then stir in 1 scoop protein powder. 3. Top with sliced banana and enjoy.

breakfast.name: Eggs with Toast
breakfast.directions: 1. Toast 2 slices of bread and butter them. 2. Fry or scramble 2-3 eggs with salt and pepper. 3. Serve eggs on or alongside toast.

breakfast.name: Greek Yogurt Bowl
breakfast.directions: 1. Scoop 1 cup Greek yogurt into bowl. 2. Drizzle with honey. 3. Top with granola and fresh berries.

breakfast.name: Protein Shake
breakfast.directions: 1. Add 1 scoop protein powder, 1 cup milk, 1 banana to blender. 2. Add ice cubes. 3. Blend until smooth and serve.

breakfast.name: Halwa Puri (Weekend)
breakfast.directions: 1. Make halwa: cook suji in ghee, add sugar and water. 2. Knead flour dough, rest 15 mins, roll and deep fry puris. 3. Serve with chana masala (chickpea curry).

breakfast.name: Nihari with Naan (Weekend)
breakfast.directions: 1. Reheat leftover nihari on stove until hot. 2. Heat naan on tawa or in oven. 3. Garnish nihari with fresh ginger slices and cilantro. Serve hot.
